comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts, locks, and cycle-checks a gripper opening stop; PR-1288 selects and installs the matching driver bit, power-tightens a loose drawer knob, and returns the stopped tool.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires concurrent wrench/driver seating and countertorque on coupled adjustment hardware; PR-1288 requires visual bit selection, bit insertion, powered screw engagement, drawer stabilization, and tool return.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate scores retained target angle, locknut seating, repeated-cycle drift, tool removal, and clearance; PR-1288 scores stable correct-bit installation, ≥1.3 mm powered screw feed, ≤0.2 mm knob gap, a 5 N hold test, and stable tool release in its stand.
comparison.reason: PR-1288 tests tool configuration and powered fastening of a loose screw, while the candidate tests preserving a tunable stop against locknut reaction and demonstrating retained articulated function. Both provide complete numeric scoring and loss conditions.
